title: Kernel preemption during prefill causes stale KV writes and intermittent softmax anomalies
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
We observed sporadic correctness regressions (logit skew / sampling divergence) on long-context decoder workloads after several kernel-selection performance changes. Failures only show up in production-like load profiles with concurrent prefill + decode mixes and when the scheduler preempts attention kernels to prioritize short-tail decode requests. Root cause hypothesis: a race between kernel preemption and the KV cache index update path leads to stale/partially-applied KV metadata which downstream kernels treat as valid. That in turn produces malformed KV lookups, silent numeric drift in softmax inputs, and eventually divergent outputs compared to baseline builds.

Symptoms observed:
- Intermittent change in token distribution for identical prompts (sampling drift) ~1 in 20k requests on affected model + config.
- Errors do not raise exceptions but result in low-magnitude numerical differences that accumulate, occasionally producing clearly incorrect generations.
- Logs show "kv_index_mismatch" warnings only when kernel routing toggles between high and low priority lanes.
- Repro harness (see attachments) can reproduce in ~1/300 runs when configured with high concurrency and mixed prefill/decode sequences.

Reproduction steps (minimal):
1) Use model: rwd-llama-70b-quant (runtime-1.22 build with new kernel_selector).
2) Run bench harness: mixed_prefill_decode_repro.py on 8-GPU dedicated pool with concurrency profile: 75% small decodes (seq_len 64) interleaved with 25% long prefill requests (seq_len 2048).
3) Enable kernel preemption feature flag (kernel_routing.preempt_short_jobs=true).
4) Observe divergent outputs or kv-index warnings in agent logs within ~1000 requests.

Investigation notes:
- The KV index update is currently a two-step non-atomic path: write KV entries, then publish index pointer. If a preemption interrupts between steps, a low-priority decode may read the old index while KV buffers are partially populated.
- Kernel selector can migrate a running attention kernel out of the compute queue to make room for short decodes. Migration does not currently quiesce in-flight KV index operations.
- Numerical drift is amplified by mixed-precision kernels; differences are small initially but softmax exponentiation magnifies them.
- We validated that forcing kernel affinity (disable preemption) eliminates the bug in the repro harness.

Proposed mitigation options (short -> long):
- Immediate: Add an atomic publish for KV index (single CAS/compare-and-swap update) so readers never see a partially-updated index. Low-risk, should be landed as a patch.
- Near-term: Add a lightweight per-sequence writer lock that prevents preemption until KV publish completes. Slightly higher perf cost but simpler to reason about.
- Medium-term: Refactor kernel preemption to quiesce critical sections (KV and KV-index updates) before migration. Requires changes to kernel runtime scheduler and testing across platforms.
- Long-term: Introduce versioned KV pointers with epoch checks in readers; readers reject stale epochs and either block or fall back to safe kernels. More complex but robust under future concurrency.

Testing plan:
- Unit tests: simulate interleaved writer/publisher/readers with mocked scheduler to assert no partial index is observed.
- Integration: run mixed_prefill_decode_repro.py with 50k runs; target is zero reproductions for the patch.
- Regression suite: add a fuzzed concurrency job to CI that runs nightly on the dedicated pool.

Rollout plan:
1) Land atomic publish patch behind feature flag (kernel_kv.atomic_publish=true) and run 72h canary against dedicated cluster.
2) If stable, flip flag on-by-default in runtime-1.22.
3) Monitor token-level divergence metric and kv-index warning rate in Console dashboards.

Notes and links:
- Repro harness: internal drive link: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/repro/mixed_prefill_decode_repro
- Initial log snippet and trigram diff: https://logs.redwood.ai/queries/kv_index_mismatch/ENG-24681
- Related tickets: ENG-21234 (kv-index corruption investigation), ENG-20412 (interleaving kernel priority stale-kvindex)

Risks/Trade-offs:
- Atomic publish will slightly increase median prefill latency because of cache-line atomic operations, but eliminates correctness risk.
- Introducing per-seq locks will reduce concurrency; we should measure throughput impact and consider adaptive lock elision for low-contention paths.
- Larger scheduler refactor has higher engineering cost but will future-proof for more aggressive preemption strategies.

Decision so far:
- Implement atomic KV index publish as a first patch (PR referenced below). If metrics show unacceptable performance regressions, iterate with per-seq writer lock as a fallback.
